facts.label: Passivo no presente
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + participle: Tickets are sold. The concert is held outside. Bags are checked at the entrance.

facts.label: Am/is/are + particípio
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + particípio quando o foco é a coisa: Tickets are sold here. The concert is held outside. Use is no singular e are no plural.

facts.label: Perguntas no passivo
facts.sub: Inverta is/are e o sujeito: Is food allowed? Are children’s tickets sold? Respostas curtas: Yes, it is. No, they aren’t.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “os ingressos são vendidos” e “as bolsas são revistadas”.
compare.us: Em inglês, o passivo no presente usa am/is/are + particípio: Tickets are sold. The concert is held outside. Bags are checked.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The passive present is am/is/are + participle.
We say “Tickets sell at the door” for the passive.
items.why: We say Tickets are sold at the door.

items.s: We use is with singular nouns.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The passive present is am/is/are + participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Tickets sell at the door” for the passive. → Falso (We say Tickets are sold at the door.)
We use is with singular nouns. → Verdadeiro (The concert is held outside.)

pages.title: A concert near the beach in Miami · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot evening in Miami. Marco meets his friend Ela near a big stage. A large crowd waits outside. The sun goes down over the beach. Ela already has a place in the line. Marco still needs tickets.

“Marco, hurry! The tickets are almost sold out.” says Ela. “Really? How many tickets are sold every day?” says Marco. “About two hundred. They are sold on the website and at the box office.” says Ela.
